findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A repo's root package.json permits pnpm >=9 <11, while web/package.json requires pnpm ^9 and web/pnpm-lock.yaml is its only pnpm lockfile.
The root engine takes precedence over the nested engine, so the generated setup step requests >=9 <11 and installs pnpm 10. An install in web then fails its ^9 engine check, even though pnpm 9 satisfies both manifests. The lookup also ignores a nested packageManager or devEngines.packageManager pin, so a pnpm 9 pin with a format-9 lockfile renders version 10. The snapshot agrees with this incorrect render, leaving the previous version finding open while the upgrade skips review. [pnpm documents the engine check](https://pnpm.io/10.x/package_json#engines).

why: The upgrade check renders the generated workflow from a snapshot folder with no git repo, so a client repo whose only pnpm lockfile is in a subfolder gets a render without the pnpm setup step, the render differs from the committed workflow, and a pure upgrade then gets a model review.
